channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gains as high inflation fuels odds of RBNZ September rate hikes
item.description: NZD/USD gains ground after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 0.5960 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold retreats from mid-May highs; fails ahead of $4,700 as Fed risks support USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) touched a fresh high since May 14, during the Asian session on Tuesday, though it struggled to capitalize on the move and failed to break the $4,700 mark.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Will focus on key policies in FY27 budget to drive economic growth
item.description: Japan Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama said in the Asian trading session on Tuesday that the government aims to balance fiscal sustainability and economic growth and communicate with markets on this stance.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains steady following RBA Meeting Minutes
item.description: AUD/USD gains ground after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around 0.7150 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: WTI holds ground above $84.50 as escalating concerns over US sanctions on Iran
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price appreciates after registering over 2% losses in the previous day, trading around $84.70 per barrel during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: RBA Minutes: Board ready to raise rates if upside risks materialise
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) published the Minutes of its July monetary policy meeting on Tuesday, with the key takeaways noted below.

item.title: Iran’s Economy Minister Madanizadeh: Enemies should wait for an attack
item.description: Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said on Tuesday, "We are fully prepared for the US sanctions."

item.title: Japanese Yen consolidates around 159.00 vs USD as bearish potential remains intact
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is seen oscillating in a narrow band just above the 159.00 mark during the Asian session on Tuesday, awaiting a fresh catalyst before the next leg of a directional move.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7852 vs. 6.7841 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7852 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7841 and 6.7219 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro gains support amid hawkish ECB expectations, subdued US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD inches higher after posting minor losses in the previous day, trading around 1.1670 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair finds support as rising oil prices, elevated bond yields, and escalating Middle East tensions drive Eurozone inflation concerns.

item.title: Australian Dollar falls as Iran sanctions sour risk appetite, RBA minutes eyed
item.description: The Australian Dollar began the week on a lower note, trading with a 0.28% loss against the Greenback as risk appetite soured after the US Department of the Treasury imposed sanctions on Iran-linked entities. At the time of writing, the pair trades at 0.7159

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Targeting 6.7200 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann keep a downside bias on USD/CNH after the pair dipped to 6.7180 and closed near 6.7210.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Bulls struggle at 187 amid intervention fears
item.description: The EUR/JPY trades horizontally on Monday as market participants remain reluctant to push the cross higher amid fears of potential intervention by Japanese authorities, even though they have remained shut following the coordinated action by the US and Japan.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: 217.00 caps bulls as RSI stalls
item.description: The GBP/JPY consolidates near familiar levels around 217.00 on Monday, as risk aversion dominates markets, with flows moving into haven assets like the US Dollar and Gold amid uncertainty over the Middle East conflict.

item.title: South Korean Won: Rally faces consolidation risk on policy week – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that South Korean Won (KRW) has extended its rally, with USD/KRW briefly touching 1380 on exporter and corporate US Dollar (USD) selling and a softer USD backdrop.

item.title: Record intervention bought the Japanese Yen three weeks
item.description: Dollar-Yen holds near 159.00 into the North American afternoon, marginally higher on the day inside a range of roughly three quarters of a Yen between the 158.50 area and a high short of 159.50.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: 1.1700 caps bulls as RSI overheats
item.description: The shared currency registers minimal losses of 0.13% versus the US Dollar as EUR/USD fails to surpass 1.1700, exacerbating the drop towards the 1.1660 area, despite retaining its current neutral-to-upward bias.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar muted near multi-month highs as it outweighs soft retail sales
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is holding firm against the US Dollar (USD) at the time of writing, with NZD/USD consolidating near its recent multi-month highs, just south of the 0.6000 handle.

item.title: British Pound Sterling climbs on a problem it has worse
item.description: Sterling holds just above 1.3600 into the North American afternoon, marginally lower on the day and inside a range of barely 35 pips, having printed a five-month high short of 1.3700 late last week.

item.title: Japanese Yen lower as US Dollar firms on heavier Iran sanctions
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is grinding higher against the Japanese Yen (JPY) at the time of writing, with USD/JPY holding north of the 159.00 mark.

item.title: Singapore: National Day Rally focus – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Chua Han Teng reviews Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s National Day Rally 2026, highlighting policy themes rather than markets.

item.title: Asia FX: Mixed central bank paths shape THB, KRW, PHP – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects the Bank of Thailand (BoT) to hold rates at 1.00%, leaving negative real yields that keep Thai Baht (THB) lagging. The Bank of Korea (BoK) is seen hiking again to 3.00%, supporting South Korean Won (KRW) as growth and inflation exceed targets.

item.title: Mexican Peso weakens as Iran sanctions offset Mexico’s inflation data
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) loses ground against the Greenback on Monday, even though economic data showed that inflation accelerated in the first half of August, while economic growth was softer than expected. Consequently, the USD/MXN pair trades with gains of over 0.25% to 16.96.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar firms on safe-haven demand ahead of data-heavy Tuesday
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) reclaimed the 99.00 mark for the first time since last Wednesday's plunge.

item.title: South Korean Won: Consolidation zone eyed against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao highlight South Korea’s strong export-led growth and large current-account surplus as key drivers of Korean Won strength against the Dollar.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Cautious rebound capped near 100 – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret observe that the US Dollar (USD) is modestly stronger as markets start the week cautiously, with equities defensive and Treasuries firmer.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Gradual appreciation bias with key levels against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that RMB and CNH remain supported by softer USD dynamics and exporter conversion, but the People’s Bank of China is signalling a preference for gradual gains via its fixing.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG pullback tests 100-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price reverses course on Monday, down 0.59% as buyers failed to push the white metal past $70.00, which exacerbated a reversal to the first support level at the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) at $68.42. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades at $68.52, after peaking at $69.92.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Upside risk stays intact against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann maintain a cautious stance on USD/SGD after Friday’s drop to 1.2682 and close near 1.2700.

item.title: Gold rallies as Iran sanctions stoke haven demand
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price resumes its advance on Monday and refreshes three-month highs at $4,681 as US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent crosses the wires to reveal sanctions on Iran-linked entities, while investors await a speech by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday.
